edges.description: Cat scratches or bites introduce B. henselae through a local skin wound.
Inoculation leads to draining regional lymphadenitis.
Inflamed draining lymph nodes present as regional lymphadenopathy.
The host response to Bartonella infection can produce fever.
Some patients develop systemic organ involvement rather than isolated nodal disease.
Severe disseminated CSD can involve bone as osteomyelitis.
Ocular CSD can involve the optic nerve and retina.
Disseminated Bartonella infection can involve the central nervous system.
Disseminated complicated CSD can involve bone as osteomyelitis.
Ocular CSD can involve the optic nerve and retina as neuroretinitis.

nodes.description: In a subset of patients, CSD disseminates beyond regional lymph nodes, producing splenomegaly and hepatic or splenic microabscesses on imaging.

evidence.reference_title: Cat Scratch Disease: 9 Years of Experience at a Pediatric Center.
evidence.snippet: Among children with radiographic imaging, 20 of 55 (36.4%) had splenomegaly and 21 of 55 (38.1%) had splenic and/or hepatic microabscesses.

evidence.snippet: The prognosis for immunocompetent patients is favorable with complete recovery, however, immunocompromised adults can progress to life-threatening complications such as neuroretinitis, osteomyelitis, and bacillary angiomatosis.
